accepted_recoveries: Scale the benchmark-owned stale canary to zero and preserve its manifest for rollback.
Increase the namespace CPU quota by the minimum required amount when cluster capacity and policy permit it.
forbidden_actions: Do not delete or scale down unrelated tenant workloads.
Do not remove the ResourceQuota object.
Do not reduce checkout resource requests below measured safe requirements merely to pass admission.
incident.injected_fault: A benchmark-owned stale canary reserves the remaining namespace CPU request quota, so new checkout replicas are rejected even though cluster nodes have capacity.
observable_signals: Checkout ReplicaSet events report exceeded quota for requests.cpu.
ResourceQuota status shows requested CPU at its hard limit.
Nodes retain enough allocatable CPU for the rejected replicas.
preconditions: The stale canary is labeled as benchmark-owned and has zero live traffic.
Worker nodes have capacity for the intended checkout replicas.
No LimitRange or scheduler constraint independently blocks the rollout.
required_evidence: Capture ResourceQuota hard and used values.
Attribute namespace CPU requests to their owning workloads.
Show that the stale canary is benchmark-owned and receives no traffic before reclaiming its quota.
incident.title: ResourceQuota saturation

payload.answer: Scale down the benchmark-owned stale canary deployment to 0 replicas to release CPU quota for checkout-api.

The incident CASE-06 (ResourceQuota saturation) in namespace proofix-case-06 is resolved. The ResourceQuota 'case-06-cpu-budget' was saturated at 500m requests.cpu (hard: 500m, used: 500m), preventing checkout-api from scaling to its desired 3 replicas (each requesting 100m CPU). The namespace CPU request quota was consumed by two running checkout-api pods (2x100m = 200m) and one benchmark-owned stale canary pod (300m CPU request) labeled with 'proofix.io/benchmark-owned: true' and 'proofix.io/live-traffic: false'. By scaling deployment/stale-canary to 0 replicas, 300m CPU request quota was reclaimed, allowing checkout-api's third replica to be admitted and scheduled on node vm-4 without modifying the ResourceQuota object or reducing safe container resource requests.

critical_claims.claim: ResourceQuota 'case-06-cpu-budget' hard limit is 500m requests.cpu and was fully used at 500m requests.cpu.
Namespace CPU requests were attributed to checkout-api (2 pods requesting 100m CPU each, total 200m) and stale-canary (1 pod requesting 300m CPU), totaling 500m.
ReplicaSet admission failures occurred because new pods exceeded quota: case-06-cpu-budget (requested: requests.cpu=100m, used: requests.cpu=500m, limited: requests.cpu=500m).

The stale-canary workload is confirmed to be benchmark-owned (proofix.io/benchmark-owned: 'true') and receives zero live traffic (proofix.io/live-traffic: 'false') before its quota was reclaimed by scaling it to zero.
